text:
velma: heads-up from onboarding smoke: rust-sdk json-mode fncall sanitizer is dropping explicit nulls when schema has `additionalProperties: false` and a union that includes array|null. sample-app logs show downstream code getting `{}` instead of null which causes type errors in handlers.

ion: ouch. can you paste the minimal schema + the exact raw model output you saw?

velma: minimal schema (trimmed):
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "response": {
      "oneOf": [
        {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        {"type": "null"}
      ],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  }
}
```
raw model output observed: `{"response": null}`

prasanna: and rust sanitizer turned that into `{ "response": {} }` ? how did it end up an object?

velma: yes, the sanitizer path that enforces `additionalProperties: false` ran before the union discriminator/branch resolution. when it saw `null` it normalized to an empty object as part of an internal fill-step to ensure the shape matched the allowed props and then later branch matching picked the array branch fallback resulting in `[]` or `{}` depending on downstream coercions. basically a bad ordering of normalization steps.

ion: yikes. that's different from our JS/TS behavior which preserves null and only fabricates shapes when `default` exists. looks like rust sanitizer tried to be too helpful.

sdk-qa: repro steps? we should have a tiny smoke test in sample-app runner.

velma: repro: run sample-app onboarding fncall in json-mode with that schema and a stubbed model returning `{"response": null}`. observe sanitizer logs: "normalizer.fill_missing_object -> {}" then "branch picker -> array matched -> coerced to []".

prasanna: suggested fix: 1) change sanitizer ordering so union branch decision happens BEFORE enforcing `additionalProperties`/fill steps; 2) treat literal null as a first-class branch value and short-circuit normalization if original raw JSON had `null` (unless schema explicitly has `default` or `nullable: false` semantics).

ion: add a feature flag `legacy_shape_fill` default off for new installs so we can opt-in older templates during rollout. also add telemetry count for how often sanitizer would have filled shapes so we can measure impact.

velma: PR created: https://git.redwood/s/sdk-rust/fix/null-preserve-then-filter (WIP). included unit tests and an integration smoke that runs sample-app onboarding.

ci-bot: CI queued for PR fix/null-preserve-then-filter  build 11457. samplekit/onboard-integration suite will run.

prasanna: tests to add: union[array,null] with raw null -> expect preserved null; union[array,object] with raw null -> expect null preserved; also case where server-side shim might translate null -> {} (ENGRT-1001) so add an end-to-end that includes server-side compatibility check.

ion: good call. also add an auth/retry combinator test: simulate a 401 then retry returning full body with null -> ensure sanitizer only runs on final full body and not on intermediate truncated body. we had a flaky in the past where sanitizer processed truncated payload.

velma: added both tests. CI failed on a flaky samplekit runner unrelated; retriggered and then green. PR merged. releasing rust-sdk v0.1.2.

sdk-qa: can you open a follow-up ticket to parity-check the same sanitizer ordering in py/js/go/dotnet? DEVEX-3650 maybe.

prasanna: filed DEVEX-3650 "sanitizer ordering parity: preserve nulls prior to shape-fill enforcement" and assigned to sdk-parity.

velma: rolling a short note to onboarding teams and updating the starter templates to pin sdk-rust v0.1.2 so new users avoid the break.

ion: nice work. final nit: update SDK README "json-mode sanitization" section describing the exact ordering: 1) literal value preservation, 2) union/branch resolution, 3) shape-fill and additionalProperties enforcement. helps integrators reason about behavior.

prasanna: docs updated in PR. closing thread. thanks all! :tada:
